work.title: The First Part of Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Flourish. Enter on the walls La Pucelle, Charles, Reignier, Alençon and Soldiers.

lines.text: Advance our waving colours on the walls;
lines.plainText: Advance our waving colours on the walls

lines.text: Rescued is Orleans from the English.
lines.plainText: Rescued is Orleans from the English

lines.text: Thus Joan la Pucelle hath perform'd her word.
lines.plainText: Thus Joan la Pucelle hath perform'd her word

lines.text: Divinest creature, Astraea's daughter,
lines.plainText: Divinest creature Astraea's daughter

lines.text: How shall I honour thee for this success?
lines.plainText: How shall I honour thee for this success

lines.text: Thy promises are like Adonis' gardens
lines.plainText: Thy promises are like Adonis' gardens

lines.text: That one day bloom'd and fruitful were the next.
lines.plainText: That one day bloom'd and fruitful were the next

lines.text: France, triumph in thy glorious prophetess!
lines.plainText: France triumph in thy glorious prophetess

lines.text: Recover'd is the town of Orleans.
lines.plainText: Recover'd is the town of Orleans

lines.text: More blessed hap did ne'er befall our state.
lines.plainText: More blessed hap did ne'er befall our state

lines.text: Why ring not bells aloud throughout the town?
lines.plainText: Why ring not bells aloud throughout the town

lines.text: Dauphin, command the citizens make bonfires
lines.plainText: Dauphin command the citizens make bonfires

lines.text: And feast and banquet in the open streets
lines.plainText: And feast and banquet in the open streets

lines.text: To celebrate the joy that God hath given us.
lines.plainText: To celebrate the joy that God hath given us

lines.text: 'Tis Joan, not we, by whom the day is won;
lines.plainText: 'Tis Joan not we by whom the day is won

lines.text: For which I will divide my crown with her,
lines.plainText: For which I will divide my crown with her

lines.text: And all the priests and friars in my realm
lines.plainText: And all the priests and friars in my realm

lines.text: Shall in procession sing her endless praise.
lines.plainText: Shall in procession sing her endless praise

lines.text: A statelier pyramis to her I'll rear
lines.plainText: A statelier pyramis to her I'll rear

lines.text: Than Rhodope's of Memphis ever was;
lines.plainText: Than Rhodope's of Memphis ever was

lines.text: In memory of her when she is dead,
lines.plainText: In memory of her when she is dead

lines.text: Her ashes, in an urn more precious
lines.plainText: Her ashes in an urn more precious

lines.text: Than the rich-jewel'd coffer of Darius,
lines.plainText: Than the richjewel'd coffer of Darius

lines.text: Transported shall be at high festivals
lines.plainText: Transported shall be at high festivals

lines.text: Before the kings and queens of France.
lines.plainText: Before the kings and queens of France

lines.text: No longer on Saint Denis will we cry,
lines.plainText: No longer on Saint Denis will we cry

lines.text: But Joan la Pucelle shall be France's saint.
lines.plainText: But Joan la Pucelle shall be France's saint

lines.text: Come in, and let us banquet royally
lines.plainText: Come in and let us banquet royally

lines.text: After this golden day of victory.
lines.plainText: After this golden day of victory
